text.title: Discovery to Delivery Handover Protocol Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules with rationale + source for discovery-to-delivery-handover-protocol. Includes terminal skip-this-methodology rule.

rule.statement: Handover MUST include nine artefacts: discovery report, SoW with redlines, assumption register, risk register, stakeholder map, glossary, integration list, NFR table, open questions log. Missing any artefact blocks handover.
rule.rationale: The nine artefacts are not equally attractive to hand over. The discovery report and the SoW are the ones the pre-sales BA is proud of; the assumption register, the NFR table and the open questions log are where the contractual risk actually sits, and those are exactly the ones quietly skipped when handover is a best-effort gesture. Making the bundle blocking removes the discretion.

rule.statement: Handover MUST include a synchronous walkthrough session of at least 90 minutes with the delivery BA, the pre-sales BA, and the delivery PM; email-only handover is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Written artefacts encode the decisions but not the alternatives rejected along the way. The delivery BA inherits conclusions with no way to distinguish a hard-won constraint from an arbitrary choice, and re-opens settled questions with the client, which reads to the client as the vendor not knowing its own scope. A live session is the only channel for the discarded branches, because they exist nowhere but in the pre-sales BA's head.

rule.statement: Delivery BA MUST sign a written acknowledgement that lists every artefact received and every assumption understood; the signed document is filed with the SoW.
rule.rationale: Handover without a receipt has no completion point, so each BA keeps believing the other still owns the open questions. An itemised signature forces the delivery BA to actually open every artefact before signing, which is when missing or incomprehensible material gets found, while the pre-sales BA is still reachable rather than three months later when the client asks why an assumption was never verified.

rule.statement: Pre-sales BA remains on a hot-line (named channel, defined SLA) for 30 calendar days post-handover; questions are logged and used to update the discovery playbook.
rule.rationale: Discovery context that was never written down surfaces as questions only once delivery reaches the specifics, which is weeks after the handover meeting. With no named channel and no SLA those questions route through an account manager or die, and the delivery BA guesses instead. Logging them also shows what discovery consistently fails to capture, which is the only way the discovery playbook improves.

rule.statement: Every assumption in the register MUST be either CONFIRMED (with client sign-off ref), CONDITIONAL (with named trigger), or UNVERIFIED (with mitigation plan); ambiguous 'noted' status is forbidden.
rule.rationale: A status of noted hides the one thing that matters, which is who is on the hook if the assumption turns out false. Forcing confirmed, conditional or unverified attaches a different obligation to each: a client reference, a trigger to watch, or a mitigation to fund. Delivery can then price the residual risk instead of inheriting a flat list where everything looks equally settled.

rule.statement: Any delta between discovery findings and delivery setup MUST be logged as a change request, not silently absorbed; deltas become input to the next QBR.
rule.rationale: Each individual delta is cheaper to absorb than to document, which is precisely why they accumulate until the delivered system no longer matches the sold one and no single change can be pointed at. Routing every delta through change control keeps the commercial baseline aligned with reality, and gives the QBR a factual record of how far discovery drifted instead of a dispute.

rule.statement: Within 5 business days of handover the delivery BA is introduced in writing to every named client-side stakeholder; ghost-introductions are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Client stakeholders answer questions from people their own sponsor has vouched for. With no written introduction, the delivery BA's first contact reads as a cold approach from an unknown vendor employee, and response times collapse during exactly the weeks when requirements clarification is most time-critical. Doing it within five days spends the pre-sales BA's credibility while it is still current.

rule.statement: If there is no personnel change between discovery and delivery, return `skipped`.
rule.rationale: Every mechanism here exists to move context between two heads. When discovery and delivery are the same person the context never left, so the bundle, the walkthrough and the signed acknowledgement cost real days and transfer nothing.
